mechanism_narrative: The persistent decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates weaker weekday trip generation, so retail visits will keep falling over the next four weeks as fewer commuters pass through commercial areas.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain below their current 4-week averages for the full next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated above +25%, discretionary shopping is displaced toward at-home routines and local errand consolidation, which suppresses RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 25 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the last 28 days after RESIDENTIAL remains above 25 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS and TRANSIT both weaken together, it signals broader suppression of out-of-home circulation, and retail recreation follows with a one-week lag because leisure-linked trips are cut first.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -70 while TRANSIT is below -69
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after PARKS and TRANSIT are simultaneously below the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in WORKPLACES combined with less time at home means reopening and commuting are expanding, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks through more lunchtime and after-work shopping.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 2 points from its four-week average while RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1 point
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES rising and RESIDENTIAL falling relative to their four-week averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong PARKS signal indicates warm-weather and leisure demand, and that spillover raises nearby retail shopping within two weeks as households combine outdoor trips with consumer errands.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase relative to the last 28 days during periods when PARKS stays materially less negative than -65 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM keeps falling more negative while RESIDENTIAL stays high, households are concentrating trips on essentials and avoiding discretionary shopping, which depresses retail recreation within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines by at least 3 points over two weeks while RESIDENTIAL stays above 25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM weakens further and RESIDENTIAL remains above 25.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run rebound in TRANSIT is an early indicator of higher downtown circulation, so retail recreation should improve within one week if transit mobility stops deteriorating.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases week-on-week after being below -69
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the week following a week-on-week increase in TRANSIT from below -69.

mechanism_narrative: During tightened restrictions, simultaneous weakness in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates reduced access to city-center commerce, so retail recreation will be lower over the next four weeks than over the previous four.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain below -65 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stay below -65 for two consecutive weeks.
